3.question: What function does the social institution of the family perform?

options.B: Passing laws and monitoring their implementation

103.question: The nuclear family in the classification by composition includes...

options.A: a husband, a wife and their children
options.C: a husband with several wives and children
options.D: several brothers with wives and children

104.question: The distinguishing feature of a household compared with a family is that it...

options.A: is based only on the blood kinship of all of its members
options.C: unites people by shared domestic life, not requiring kinship
options.D: exists only in rural areas and small towns
options.E: always consists of three generations of relatives

105.question: The extended family differs from the nuclear family in that it includes...

options.E: neighbors in the community and friends of the family

106.question: The rules prescribing the choice of a marriage partner outside a certain group are called...

options.A: a form of marriage of one woman to several husbands
options.B: a union of one man and several women at the same time
options.C: successive marriages of one person to different partners
options.D: the rule of marrying within one's own social group
options.E: a group marriage of several men and several women

108.question: Which function of the family does the passing on of norms of behavior and values to children belong to?

109.question: Microsociological analysis of the family focuses on the fact that...

options.A: the family is studied as an institution in a system of other institutions
options.B: the family is regarded as a subsystem for the country's economy
options.C: the dynamics of marriages and divorces in society is analyzed
options.D: the family is studied as a small group: its formation, development and dissolution
options.E: the family serves as the basis of the class structure of society

110.question: At the macrosociological level the family is studied as...

options.A: a small autonomous group with a life cycle
options.B: a network of roles and emotional ties between spouses
options.C: a social institution in the system of other institutions of society
options.D: an association of people sharing a household without kinship
options.E: a biological group of blood relatives
